strengths: The method addresses a useful computer vision problem and demonstrates practical dataset distillation at ImageNet-1K scale using pretrained features and per-class BatchNorm regularization.

Table I reports meaningful improvements over the strengthened SRe²L replication: ImageNet accuracy increases from 54.4% to 57.6% at 50 images per class and from 58.3% to 60.7% at 100 images per class.
Experiments cover three datasets, several compression budgets, repeated evaluations, component ablations, regularization sensitivity, and transfer to larger ResNets.

The authors transparently report their improved baseline replication, explicitly credit SRe²L and the underlying optimal-transport methods/software, and provide useful recovery hyperparameters in the appendix.
weaknesses: The central mathematical contribution is insufficiently distinguished from standard quantization. Equation 4 approximates one empirical distribution per class using fewer support points. For the stated unregularized squared-Euclidean Wasserstein objective with freely optimized masses, this reduces to k-means quantization. This equivalence is not discussed, and matched k-means-target and MMD baselines are missing, leaving the claimed Wasserstein-specific advantage unestablished.

Table III attributes most of the 10-IPC improvement to per-class BatchNorm. Without barycenter matching, CE plus per-class BN achieves 64.0/41.3/37.4%, versus the full method's 64.8/41.8/38.2%. Holding CE fixed, adding barycenter matching changes accuracy by only -0.1/+0.8/+0.5 percentage points. These results support the combined pipeline more strongly than the paper's emphasis on Wasserstein matching; corresponding ablations at larger budgets are absent.

The relationship between the optimized measure and the delivered training set is unclear. Equation 3 and Algorithms 2–3 learn nonuniform masses, but Algorithm 1 outputs only images and Equations 5–7 do not incorporate those masses; weighted student sampling is also unspecified. Additionally, the text claims entropic regularization while the appendix presents unregularized transport programs without specifying an entropy coefficient. These gaps affect technical interpretation and reproducibility.

The claimed preservation of computational efficiency is inadequately measured. Table IV profiles one synthesis update on 64×64 ImageNette without comparative timings or the cost of barycenter computation. The appendix's approximately 14-hour ImageNet run provides neither a stage breakdown nor a matched baseline, preventing assessment of the full computational tradeoff.

The claims of improved distribution coverage and reduced shortcut learning exceed the evidence. Selected image examples and t-SNE plots obtained through models trained on real/synthetic mixtures provide suggestive qualitative evidence, but no quantitative coverage or robustness evaluation. Table II also lacks baseline transfer results, so it does not establish improved cross-architecture generalization over SRe²L.
